Name: rising costs
Title: Rising Costs in Japan's Domestic Agriculture
Experiment: We explore the the issue of rising cost in agriculture in Japan, and how the local farmers are threatened by increasingly higher quality and cheaper products from abroad.

Name: advanced_tech_integration
Title: Integrating Advanced Technologies in Japan's Healthcare and Eldercare Sectors
Experiment: We will explore the feasibility and impact of policies aimed at encouraging the integration of AI and robotics into healthcare and eldercare. Through interviews with healthcare providers, eldercare facility managers, technology developers, and policymakers, we will identify the most critical barriers and opportunities for technological adoption. We will propose targeted incentives such as tax breaks, grants for technology adoption, and streamlined regulatory processes to facilitate this transition. Additionally, we will consider training programs to upskill workers in these sectors to operate new technologies effectively.

Name: lifelong_learning
Title: Promoting Lifelong Learning and Continuous Professional Development in Japan
Experiment: We will explore the feasibility and impact of policies aimed at promoting lifelong learning and continuous professional development among Japan's workforce. Through interviews with educators, industry leaders, policymakers, and workers, we will identify the key barriers and opportunities for lifelong learning. We will propose targeted policies such as subsidies for continuing education, tax incentives for companies that invest in employee training, and public-private partnerships to create accessible learning platforms. Additionally, we will consider specific initiatives for underrepresented groups such as women re-entering the workforce and older adults. Digital learning platforms will be emphasized to increase accessibility and flexibility for workers. We will also implement metrics and success indicators to evaluate the impact of the policies, such as tracking the number of participants in lifelong learning programs, the employment rates of those who undergo continuous professional development, and feedback from both employees and employers.
